Judgment:
1.

The present complaint is filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the
PFA Act and Rules.

Da vs Shobit Burman Etc. on 14 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196733879/
2 2.
As per the complaint, on 28.02.2008, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Shri DP.

Singh and Field Assistant (herein after referred as FA) Shri D.N. Verma under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM) Shri S.S. Parihar visited the premises of M/s Taj Milk Food Pvt Ltd 14, Lakshmi Vihar, New Nagli Sakrawati, Najafgarh Road,
New Delhi - 110043, where accused No. 1 Shobit Burman was found conducting the business of food articles stored there, including "Ghee" (ready for sale) for sale for human consumption, bearing identical label declaration.
The sample consisted of 3x1 litre sealed plastic jar of 'Ghee' taken as three sealed plastic jar as such having identical label declaration.
The sample was taken under the supervision / direction DA vs Shobit Burman etc. of Sh. S.S. Parihar, SDM/LHA.
The Food Inspector divided the sample originally packed jar of Ghee having identical label declaration in each part.
Each sample counter part containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample counter parts.
Notice in Form VI was given to accused No.1 Shobit Burman and the price of sample was also given to him.
Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.

All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused No.1 Shobit Burman and the other witness Sh.
D.N. Verma, FA.
Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh. D.N. Verma, FA was joined as witness.

3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 82/LHA/21410 was sent to Public Analyst,
Delhi in intact condition and remaining two counter-parts were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same as misbranded.

The report of the Public Analyst is as follows:
"The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Rule 32e.
The language of best before declaration is not as per Rule 32(i) of PFA Act and Rules and it is declared in a misleading manner.

However, Ghee conforms to standard"
4.

It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Shobit Burman was the vendor-cum-salesman of M/s Taj Milk Food Pvt Ltd 14, Lakshmi Vihar, New Nagli Sakrawati, Najafgarh Road, New Delhi - DA vs Shobit Burman etc. 110043, at the time of sampling and he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the company.

Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 18.02.2010 alleging violation of section 2(ix)(g)&(k) of PFA Act, 1954 and 32 (e)(f)&(i) and Rule 37 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused.
DA vs Shobit Burman etc.
6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused No. 1, 6 & 7 were summoned vide order dated 18.02.2010.

On the basis of PA report, notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of 32 (e)(f)&(i) of PFA Rules, 1955 and 2(ix)(g)&(k) of PFA Act, 1954, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
During the trial the accused No. 6 Rajesh Kumar was declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 09.09.2010.
The accused No. 7 M/s Taj Milk Foods Pvt Ltd

vide order dated 07.09.2016 was proceeded ex-parte.
7.
At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 SDM/LHA Sh S.S. Parihar, PW-2 FA Sh D.N. Verma, PW-3 FI Sh B.P. Saroha.

FI D.P. Singh and PW-3 FA Sh D.N.
Verma were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. S.S. Parihar.

These witness(except Food Inspector D.P.Singh) narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the three plastic jars of Ghee from the vendor,
bearing identical label declaration, dividing the sample commodity into three equal parts by putting one originally sealed plastic jar of Ghee as one counterpart, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.

They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt DA vs Shobit Burman etc. Ex. PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. Raid report under Rule 9(e) Ex.PW1/D was prepared at the spot.

Thereafter two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA on 29.02.2008 vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW 1/E under the intimation that one part of the same has already been deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/F.
Thereafter PA Report was received.
Thereafter, the present case file was marked to PW-3 FSO FI B.P. Saroha, who during investigation sent letter Ex. PW3/A to accused no.7 Company.
He also sent letter Ex. PW3/B to the ROC to ascertain the constitution of the said Company.
He then sent letters Ex. PW3/C and Ex. PW3/D to accused no.7 and ROC respectively seeking further details.
PW-3 FSO FI B.P. Saroha received reply Ex. PW3/E from the ROC along with documents Mark-3A disclosing that the Company had four Directors.
PW-3 FSO FI B.P. Saroha also obtained the details of accused no.7 Company from FI Ranjeet Singh who dealt with another case against accused no.7.
The said documents are Mark - 3B to 3K.
The vendor accused no.1 had also given a reply Ex. PW3/F. PW-3 FSO FI B.P. Saroha did not receive any reply from accused no.7 till filing of the complaint.
Thereafter, PW-3 FSO FI B.P. Saroha sent the file for obtaining sanction of the Director (PFA).
The then Director Sh. D. P. Dwivedi granted consent vide order Ex.
PW3 /G

After obtaining consent,
PW-3 FSO FI B.P. Saroha filed the complaint Ex. PW3/H in the Court.
Then intimation letter Ex.PW3/I(OSR) was sent to the accused persons vide postal receipts Ex.PW3/J (OSR).
Three letters Ex. PW3/K1, Ex. PW3/K2 and Ex. PW3/K3 received back undelivered.

After filing of the DA vs Shobit Burman etc. complaint, PW-3 FSO FI B.P. Saroha received reply Ex.PW3/L from accused Da vs Shobit Burman Etc. on 14 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196733879/
4 no.7 alongwith copies of Memorandum and Article of Association Ex. PW3/M1 and Ex. PW3/M2.
They also sent copy of the document pertaining to the nomination Ex. PW3/N as well as one label Ex. PW3/O.
The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence Counsel.
8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 10.03.2017 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
The accused chooses not to lead defence evidence accordingly matter was fixed for final arguments.
9. In a criminal case, the burden is only on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
10. The present case alleges adulteration in the sample of Ghee purchased from the business concern of the accused no.1.
This sample of Ghee has been analysed by PA.
11. The prosecution alleges the offence of misbranding on the basis of PA report.
As per PA report the sample was misbranded because best before declaration was written on the label in a misleading manner.
In this regard A witness CW1 was examined in court who produced a counterpart of a the sample in court.
On the label it was written that the sample was best before within 9 months from the date of DA vs Shobit Burman etc. packaging.
The defence has relied upon the judgment of S.S.Gokul Krishnan and others vs State 2009(I)FAC 132, to argue that this declaration is not misleading.

entities.text: S.S.Gokul Krishnan and others vs State 2009(I)FAC 132
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. Without going into this aspect, I am of the view that the case of the prosecution has not been proved because the most important witness of the prosecution that is the food inspector Sh.
D.P.Singh who purchased the sample and prepared all the documents in this case could not be examined as he passed away before his evidence.

13. The only witnesses are in this case are PW-3 Sh D.N. Verma, Field Assistant and SDM,
S.S.Parihar who were present on the spot along with the Food Inspector and therefore the whole case of the prosecution is based on his testimony.
Since the Food Inspector had already passed away prior to recording of his evidence, the prosecution is bereft of the most important evidence of the offence alleged.

In the absence of the testimony of Food Inspector who was visited the spot and prepared all the relevant documents, convicting the accused only on the basis of the accompanying official, that too, without any other corroboration or independent public witness would not be safe.

Reliance is placed on the judgement of State of Gujarat vs Ashokbhai (Amrutbhai) Shankardas Patel 2011(1)FAC 66, State of Gujarat vs Naranbhai Somabhai Prajapati 2010(1) FAC 603, State of Gujrat vs Ashoke Kumar Aasandas Kotak and Another 2007 (2)FAC 50, Puranmal Badrilal Gupta vs State of M.P and others 2007(1)FAC 207 and State of M.P vs Mangal Singh Criminal Appeal No. 299/1987 dated 28/02/1994.
